The conditional perfect can conjecture from a past moment: habría salido antes de nuestra llegada. Debió de salir presents a past inference. 11wbxt: Original SpanishCue material; the situations and data are for teaching purposes, not real news or official exam texts.
1oruztw: The community greenhouse woke up with several trays of plants out of place. The first explanation circulated in the message group before the coordinator arrived: someone must have come in during the night and taken some of the materials. The side door was ajar and two labels were missing. Those facts made the hypothesis of an unauthorized entry possible, but still did not allow it to be told apart from a move made by a member of the team.
hxypgs: The access log showed an opening at nine at night with the maintenance card. Its holder explained that she had gone to close a window because wind had been forecast. A photograph sent at eight thirty showed the trays next to that same window. At ten past nine, a neighbor heard a bang. No one knew whether it came from the greenhouse or from a nearby dumpster. Bringing that sound into the story as proof of a theft would have required more information than actually existed.
zo84bz: The inventory check revealed that no tools were missing. The plants were on another table and the labels turned up under a box. The maintenance person then remembered that she had moved some trays to reach the latch, although she could not be sure she had put them all back. The door will have been left badly closed, the coordinator suggested. It was a plausible explanation, not a certainty: the mechanism could also have opened because of a malfunction. They decided to check it before blaming the problem on individual carelessness.
1unwsda: The case ended without a spectacular conclusion. The latch was adjusted and a simple log was created to note movements of material. Some people felt that time had been wasted investigating a minor incident. Others pointed out that the investigation had prevented an unjustified accusation. Sometimes the usefulness of gathering evidence lies precisely in giving up an attractive story and replacing it with a more limited explanation, whose uncertainty is acknowledged rather than concealed.
